builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
summary: The method replaces the standard practice of keeping only the best-validation checkpoint from an RL (GRPO) run and discarding intermediate checkpoints; instead it treats all saved checkpoints as frozen teachers and distills their complementary capabilities into the best checkpoint via dynamic teacher selection (HCN) and locality-restricted supervision (LAD). The cost is an additional distillation stage with on-policy rollouts, teacher inference across multiple checkpoints, and selection/filtering logic, though no new RL training is required. It can fail when teacher selection mismatches the student's problem-specific gaps, when supervision is not properly localized and overwrites already-mastered behavior, or when the checkpoint pool lacks genuine complementarity.
rationale: The technique presupposes a completed multi-checkpoint GRPO/RL pipeline plus extra rollout and distillation compute, which exceeds what most constrained-infrastructure teams operate, though it is worth adopting if they already run agentic RL fine-tuning.

claims.statement: The method replaces the standard practice of keeping only the best-validation checkpoint from an RL (GRPO) run and discarding intermediate checkpoints; instead it treats all saved checkpoints as frozen teachers and distills their complementary capabilities into the best checkpoint via dynamic teacher selection (HCN) and locality-restricted supervision (LAD). The cost is an additional distillation stage with on-policy rollouts, teacher inference across multiple checkpoints, and selection/filtering logic, though no new RL training is required. It can fail when teacher selection mismatches the student's problem-specific gaps, when supervision is not properly localized and overwrites already-mastered behavior, or when the checkpoint pool lacks genuine complementarity.

Up to 7.4 points improvement over the best-validation checkpoint across five agentic domains and 24 benchmarks; a 4B student reportedly surpasses GPT-5.6 and DeepSeek-V4.1 on deep search. Point gains, not a multiplicative factor.
